BWP-L3 — complete current scientific reader

This reader preserves every scientific field in the supplied current disclosure reader, including adverse evidence, guards, limitations and retained historical layers. The earlier pending-disclosure header is a historical publication state. Read the scientific account with these records.

Named scientific-worker context identifiers and private custody locators were already replaced in the supplied disclosure reader. Those specific replacements remain. No scientific finding is withheld merely because its source was privately held.

Historical origin

Workflow-log activity assumptions in the 1990s; explicit event-data guidance in the 2011 Manifesto; later timestamp and healthcare critiques.

Lineage class

NATIVE_PROCESS_MINING_CONTRIBUTION_OR_REFINEMENT

Original form

Workflow-log activity assumptions in the 1990s; explicit event-data guidance in the 2011 Manifesto; later timestamp and healthcare critiques. The reconstructed initial problem is: A status row, a retrospective form entry and an activity execution can share a label while denoting different occurrences.

Problem it addressed

A status row, a retrospective form entry and an activity execution can share a label while denoting different occurrences.

Failure mode it tries to prevent

A status row, a retrospective form entry and an activity execution can share a label while denoting different occurrences.

Mechanism

For each event class, establish what happened or was recorded, by whom or what, at which lifecycle phase, and with what relation to an actual work episode. Test a small number of material examples against source-system behaviour and domain testimony; preserve unresolved alternatives rather than inventing execution semantics.

Trigger or context

Any claim that interprets event labels or counts as activities, transitions or work.

Non trigger or cheap path

Reuse a tested event dictionary when the recording mechanism has not changed. For a question about recorded transactions only, explicitly narrow the claim instead of reconstructing an entire process.

Dependencies or preconditions

Access to event definitions or source examples; someone able to explain recording practice; distinction between occurrence time and recording time.

Domain profile
Event semantics and source provenance

Central: event occurrence, recording act and activity execution are separate predicates; the mapping needs evidence. Record-specific application: A status row, a retrospective form entry and an activity execution can share a label while denoting different occurrences. A sampled event can be traced to an intelligible recorded occurrence; ambiguous classes are excluded, bounded or clearly labelled in results.

Case or object notion

Declare the case, encounter, object or decision unit before assessing event counts; a row identifier is not automatically the analytical unit.

Extraction abstraction and ordering

Record joins, filters, lifecycle interpretation, abstraction and ordering; preserve ambiguity where the sources do not justify one order.

Log completeness noise and selection

Assess missingness, duplicate records, selection and noise against the actual question; neither perfect-log demands nor convenient-extract acceptance is justified.

Model class and discovery assumptions

Discovery is downstream and optional. No choice of miner repairs an unjustified event-to-work interpretation by itself.

Reference model and conformance semantics

If conformance is performed, map the event vocabulary to the reference explicitly; schema validity is not conformity to the intended process.

Fitness precision generalisation and simplicity

Model quality scores are not log-validity measures. Input validity is assessed before and alongside downstream quality evaluation.

Temporal validity and drift

Version recording and extraction practices; changed instrumentation can invalidate apparently stable event semantics.

Prediction causality and intervention boundary

Correctly extracted observations can support description without identifying causal effects. Prediction additionally requires decision-time availability.

Human validation privacy and decision consumer

Use relevant source custodians and participants to test meanings; collect and retain only the detail justified by a legitimate consumer.

Expected engineering payoff
Claim

A sampled event can be traced to an intelligible recorded occurrence; ambiguous classes are excluded, bounded or clearly labelled in results.

Status

EXPECTED_OR_LOGICALLY_REQUIRED_FOR_THE_STATED_CLAIM_NOT_A_UNIVERSAL_MEASURED_BENEFIT

Cost boundary

Reuse a tested event dictionary when the recording mechanism has not changed. For a question about recorded transactions only, explicitly narrow the claim instead of reconstructing an entire process.

Actor and authority boundary

Analyst and domain participant decide whether an event class supports the proposed question; data custodians explain recording but do not determine organisational obligations. Analytical competence does not itself supply additional organisational authority.

Problem it addressed

Failure mode it tries to prevent

A reproducible diagram cannot be investigated when its events have lost source identities and transformation history.

Mechanism

Retain a feasible trace-back from a consequential output through selected events, source identifiers and extraction versions. Use protected pseudonymous keys where direct identifiers are unnecessary. Record which lineage edges cannot be reconstructed.

Trigger or context

A result may be challenged, repeated, corrected or used for consequential action.

Non trigger or cheap path

A query identifier, immutable extract and short mapping may suffice for a one-off local analysis; a full enterprise provenance platform is not required.

Original form

Database-to-event extraction became a first-class problem as mining moved beyond ready-made workflow logs. The reconstructed initial problem is: Joins, correlation rules and event selection can manufacture repeated work, exclude unfinished cases or omit relevant relationships.

Problem it addressed

Joins, correlation rules and event selection can manufacture repeated work, exclude unfinished cases or omit relevant relationships.

Failure mode it tries to prevent

Mechanism

State extraction predicates, join cardinalities, event-to-source mappings and inclusion/exclusion rules. Check material counts and sample reconciliations against the operational sources; preserve a route back to excluded or unresolved records.

Trigger or context

Events are assembled from databases, APIs, status tables or multiple systems rather than directly supplied as a tested event log.

Non trigger or cheap path

A simple, documented query is adequate where one source already contains the required event semantics. Do not build a generic integration layer merely to perform one bounded query.

Dependencies or preconditions

Knowledge of source keys, join multiplicities and lifecycle fields; snapshot or transaction-time boundaries; access to excluded-record counts.

Original form

Activity identification in workflow mining and multi-perspective simplification in Fuzzy Mining. The reconstructed initial problem is: Very fine records create uninterpretable detail; coarse labels erase distinct states, exceptions and causal alternatives.

Problem it addressed

Very fine records create uninterpretable detail; coarse labels erase distinct states, exceptions and causal alternatives.

Failure mode it tries to prevent

Very fine records create uninterpretable detail; coarse labels erase distinct states, exceptions and causal alternatives.

Mechanism

Choose an activity vocabulary at the level of the decision, retain the mapping from raw observations to abstract events, and test whether material conclusions survive a plausible finer or coarser alternative. Treat an abstract event as a derived object, not a newly observed fact.

Trigger or context

Raw logs are too fine, labels combine distinct tasks, or analysis must cross systems with different granularity.

Non trigger or cheap path

Use the native activity labels when they already answer the question. A small manually checked mapping can dominate an automated abstraction model.

Dependencies or preconditions

A declared abstraction function or rule set; ability to inspect affected records; awareness of many-to-one and one-to-many mappings.

Domain profile
Event semantics and source provenance

Primary concern: distinguish a recording act from the work it denotes; retain source identity sufficient for material trace-back. Record-specific application: Very fine records create uninterpretable detail; coarse labels erase distinct states, exceptions and causal alternatives. A material finding states its abstraction level and has a traceable mapping and sensitivity result.

Case or object notion

Declare the case, encounter, object or decision unit before assessing event counts; a row identifier is not automatically the analytical unit.

Extraction abstraction and ordering

Central: preserve raw-to-abstract mapping and distinguish simplification from observed absence.

Log completeness noise and selection

Assess missingness, duplicate records, selection and noise against the actual question; neither perfect-log demands nor convenient-extract acceptance is justified.

Model class and discovery assumptions

Discovery is downstream and optional. No choice of miner repairs an unjustified event-to-work interpretation by itself.

Reference model and conformance semantics

If conformance is performed, map the event vocabulary to the reference explicitly; schema validity is not conformity to the intended process.

Fitness precision generalisation and simplicity

Model quality scores are not log-validity measures. Input validity is assessed before and alongside downstream quality evaluation.

Temporal validity and drift

Version recording and extraction practices; changed instrumentation can invalidate apparently stable event semantics.

Prediction causality and intervention boundary

Correctly extracted observations can support description without identifying causal effects. Prediction additionally requires decision-time availability.

Human validation privacy and decision consumer

Use relevant source custodians and participants to test meanings; collect and retain only the detail justified by a legitimate consumer.

Original form

Start/complete lifecycle attributes in event logs; subsequent performance analyses of intervals and queues. The reconstructed initial problem is: A completion timestamp alone is mistaken for work duration, or start/complete records are counted as separate full tasks.

Problem it addressed

A completion timestamp alone is mistaken for work duration, or start/complete records are counted as separate full tasks.

Failure mode it tries to prevent

A completion timestamp alone is mistaken for work duration, or start/complete records are counted as separate full tasks.

Mechanism

Identify lifecycle phases and pairing rules; separate enabled, started, suspended, resumed and completed states where actually observed. Compute service or waiting intervals only from phases whose meaning supports them, and label unobserved intervals as unknown.

Trigger or context

Timing, utilisation, waiting, overlapping work or activity counts depend on lifecycle interpretation.

Non trigger or cheap path

Report elapsed time between recorded milestones when service-time evidence is absent; do not impute a work interval merely to fill a dashboard.

Dependencies or preconditions

Compatible activity-instance identifiers or justified pairing; clock interpretation; treatment of cancellation and unfinished instances.

Mechanism

Use the strongest ordering supported by the evidence: a total order where justified, an explicit partial order or bounded alternatives otherwise. Keep tie-breaking separate from observed chronology and test sensitivity when an algorithm requires a sequence.

Trigger or context

Timestamp ties, mixed granularity, asynchronous systems, uncertain timestamps or consequential order-sensitive findings.

Non trigger or cheap path

Ignore order for an order-insensitive question, or flag the few ambiguous pairs instead of enumerating every possible trace.

Dependencies or preconditions

NATIVE_PROCESS_MINING_CONTRIBUTION_OR_REFINEMENT

Original form

Data-quality correction in practice; later metric, imperfection-pattern and uncertain-event research. The reconstructed initial problem is: Missing values, duplicates and errors distort models, but aggressive cleaning erases genuine exceptions and the evidence of uncertainty.

Problem it addressed

Missing values, duplicates and errors distort models, but aggressive cleaning erases genuine exceptions and the evidence of uncertainty.

Failure mode it tries to prevent

Missing values, duplicates and errors distort models, but aggressive cleaning erases genuine exceptions and the evidence of uncertainty.

Mechanism

Classify suspected defects, keep the original or a recoverable trace, justify each material repair, and compare important results with unrepaired or alternative treatments. Where correction is unsupported, carry uncertainty or decline the affected inference.

Trigger or context

Detected defects materially threaten the stated question, not merely because a quality metric is nonzero.

Non trigger or cheap path

Annotate an isolated uncertain record, narrow a claim, or tolerate a known harmless defect rather than rebuild the whole log.

Dependencies or preconditions

A defect hypothesis linked to recording behaviour; safeguards against deleting meaningful cases; separate raw and derived states.

Domain profile
Event semantics and source provenance

Primary concern: distinguish a recording act from the work it denotes; retain source identity sufficient for material trace-back. Record-specific application: Missing values, duplicates and errors distort models, but aggressive cleaning erases genuine exceptions and the evidence of uncertainty. Material repairs have reasons and consequences; users can identify which conclusions require the repair to be correct.

Case or object notion

Declare the case, encounter, object or decision unit before assessing event counts; a row identifier is not automatically the analytical unit.

Extraction abstraction and ordering

Record joins, filters, lifecycle interpretation, abstraction and ordering; preserve ambiguity where the sources do not justify one order.

Log completeness noise and selection

Assess missingness, duplicate records, selection and noise against the actual question; neither perfect-log demands nor convenient-extract acceptance is justified.

Model class and discovery assumptions

Discovery is downstream and optional. No choice of miner repairs an unjustified event-to-work interpretation by itself.

Reference model and conformance semantics

If conformance is performed, map the event vocabulary to the reference explicitly; schema validity is not conformity to the intended process.

Fitness precision generalisation and simplicity

Model quality scores are not log-validity measures. Input validity is assessed before and alongside downstream quality evaluation.

Temporal validity and drift

Version recording and extraction practices; changed instrumentation can invalidate apparently stable event semantics.

Prediction causality and intervention boundary

Correctly extracted observations can support description without identifying causal effects. Prediction additionally requires decision-time availability.

Human validation privacy and decision consumer

Use relevant source custodians and participants to test meanings; collect and retain only the detail justified by a legitimate consumer.

Expected engineering payoff
Claim

Material repairs have reasons and consequences; users can identify which conclusions require the repair to be correct.

Status

EXPECTED_OR_LOGICALLY_REQUIRED_FOR_THE_STATED_CLAIM_NOT_A_UNIVERSAL_MEASURED_BENEFIT

Annotate an isolated uncertain record, narrow a claim, or tolerate a known harmless defect rather than rebuild the whole log.

Analyst and data custodian review repair rules; domain participants distinguish atypical work from recording error. Analytical competence does not itself supply additional organisational authority.

Original form

Traditional trace/case mining exposed relational extraction problems; object-centric work made case choice an explicit modelling decision. The reconstructed initial problem is: Different case identifiers reorganise the same events into different apparent paths and repetition counts.

Problem it addressed

Different case identifiers reorganise the same events into different apparent paths and repetition counts.

Failure mode it tries to prevent

Different case identifiers reorganise the same events into different apparent paths and repetition counts.

Mechanism

Select a case notion according to the question and unit of responsibility; test relevant alternative correlations. When one case cannot retain required object interactions, keep a relational/object-centric representation instead of forcing a convenient identifier.

Trigger or context

Several plausible identifiers, hierarchical cases, or interactions between orders, items, deliveries and other objects.

Non trigger or cheap path

Use one established case identifier when it captures the required relation and produces no material flattening distortion.

Dependencies or preconditions

Knowledge of object identities and event relations; a declared analysis unit; awareness of case creation and closure rules.

Domain profile
Event semantics and source provenance

Events retain identity across object participation; an event copied into several traces is not automatically several real occurrences.

Case or object notion

Central: choose case notion or typed object relations according to the question; distinguish object types, identifiers and changing relationships. Record-specific application: Different case identifiers reorganise the same events into different apparent paths and repetition counts. The chosen case notion is explicit and conclusions that change under alternatives are identified.

Extraction abstraction and ordering

Record flattening, correlation and abstraction rules and their effects on ordering and counts. Ambiguous identity is not solved by serialization.

Log completeness noise and selection

Completeness must be assessed for both events and relationships; missing object links can distort synchronisation and duration even with complete activity labels.

Model class and discovery assumptions

Use the exact case/object formalism and supported constructs; OCPNs, type-level workflow nets and identifier-aware trees are not interchangeable guarantees.

Reference model and conformance semantics

Reference semantics must match the object/identity model. Ordinary trace conformance cannot automatically certify interaction behaviour.

Fitness precision generalisation and simplicity

Additional representational detail is not universal superiority. Evaluate task adequacy, behavioural quality and human/computation cost separately.

Temporal validity and drift

Preserve identity and relation changes over time; a stable label does not prove a stable object relationship.

Prediction causality and intervention boundary

Object context may improve a predictor or diagnostic but does not identify intervention effects or grant action authority.

Human validation privacy and decision consumer

Validate identity conventions and relation meaning with custodians and consumers; rich links can increase re-identification and interpretation burden.

Expected engineering payoff
Claim

The chosen case notion is explicit and conclusions that change under alternatives are identified.

Original form

Object-centric Petri nets and OCEL’s typed event–object relations; later dynamic identity relations. The reconstructed initial problem is: A shared event affects several entities, but flattening duplicates it or loses which entities participated.

Problem it addressed

A shared event affects several entities, but flattening duplicates it or loses which entities participated.

Failure mode it tries to prevent

A shared event affects several entities, but flattening duplicates it or loses which entities participated.

Mechanism

Represent stable object identities and types, event–object participation and needed object–object relations; record qualifiers and temporal attribute changes when relevant. Preserve multiplicity instead of copying a shared event into fictional independent occurrences.

Trigger or context

Interaction itself is needed to answer the question, including synchronisation, multi-object waiting or cross-case dependencies.

Non trigger or cheap path

A relational join or explicit shared-event table may be enough; an executable object-centric net is not mandatory.

Dependencies or preconditions

Defensible identifiers, types and relation semantics; handling of identifier reuse and changing relationships.

Domain profile
Event semantics and source provenance

Events retain identity across object participation; an event copied into several traces is not automatically several real occurrences.

Case or object notion

Central: choose case notion or typed object relations according to the question; distinguish object types, identifiers and changing relationships. Record-specific application: A shared event affects several entities, but flattening duplicates it or loses which entities participated. A shared event can be counted once while its participating objects and their types remain recoverable.

Extraction abstraction and ordering

Record flattening, correlation and abstraction rules and their effects on ordering and counts. Ambiguous identity is not solved by serialization.

Log completeness noise and selection

Completeness must be assessed for both events and relationships; missing object links can distort synchronisation and duration even with complete activity labels.

Model class and discovery assumptions

Use the exact case/object formalism and supported constructs; OCPNs, type-level workflow nets and identifier-aware trees are not interchangeable guarantees.

Reference model and conformance semantics

Reference semantics must match the object/identity model. Ordinary trace conformance cannot automatically certify interaction behaviour.

Fitness precision generalisation and simplicity

Additional representational detail is not universal superiority. Evaluate task adequacy, behavioural quality and human/computation cost separately.

Temporal validity and drift

Preserve identity and relation changes over time; a stable label does not prove a stable object relationship.

Prediction causality and intervention boundary

Object context may improve a predictor or diagnostic but does not identify intervention effects or grant action authority.

Human validation privacy and decision consumer

Validate identity conventions and relation meaning with custodians and consumers; rich links can increase re-identification and interpretation burden.

Expected engineering payoff
Claim

A shared event can be counted once while its participating objects and their types remain recoverable.

NATIVE_PROCESS_MINING_CONTRIBUTION_OR_REFINEMENT

Original form

Abstraction-oriented mining and the contemporary object-centric research agenda. The reconstructed initial problem is: A richer model increases representational coverage while becoming harder to collect, understand, validate or operate.

Problem it addressed

A richer model increases representational coverage while becoming harder to collect, understand, validate or operate.

Failure mode it tries to prevent

A richer model increases representational coverage while becoming harder to collect, understand, validate or operate.

Mechanism

Compare candidate representations against the actual distinction required, data availability, interpretation burden and computational cost. Prefer the least costly representation that preserves the consequential relation, not necessarily the fewest nodes.

Trigger or context

Choice between case-centric, object-centric, declarative, local, high-level or executable representations.

Non trigger or cheap path

Retain a tested existing view when added expressiveness would not change a decision.

Dependencies or preconditions

An identified consumer and task; assessment of what each representation omits; relevant resource constraints.

Domain profile
Event semantics and source provenance

Events retain identity across object participation; an event copied into several traces is not automatically several real occurrences.

Case or object notion

Central: choose case notion or typed object relations according to the question; distinguish object types, identifiers and changing relationships. Record-specific application: A richer model increases representational coverage while becoming harder to collect, understand, validate or operate. The selected representation has a stated advantage over a cheaper adequate alternative and a known loss boundary.

Extraction abstraction and ordering

Record flattening, correlation and abstraction rules and their effects on ordering and counts. Ambiguous identity is not solved by serialization.

Log completeness noise and selection

Completeness must be assessed for both events and relationships; missing object links can distort synchronisation and duration even with complete activity labels.

Model class and discovery assumptions

Use the exact case/object formalism and supported constructs; OCPNs, type-level workflow nets and identifier-aware trees are not interchangeable guarantees.

Reference model and conformance semantics

Reference semantics must match the object/identity model. Ordinary trace conformance cannot automatically certify interaction behaviour.

Fitness precision generalisation and simplicity

Additional representational detail is not universal superiority. Evaluate task adequacy, behavioural quality and human/computation cost separately.

Temporal validity and drift

Preserve identity and relation changes over time; a stable label does not prove a stable object relationship.

Prediction causality and intervention boundary

Object context may improve a predictor or diagnostic but does not identify intervention effects or grant action authority.

Human validation privacy and decision consumer

Validate identity conventions and relation meaning with custodians and consumers; rich links can increase re-identification and interpretation burden.

Expected engineering payoff
Claim

The selected representation has a stated advantage over a cheaper adequate alternative and a known loss boundary.

Note

Historical origin

Plural 1990s discovery approaches; explicit modelling assumptions in alpha, inductive, region-based and declarative methods.

Lineage class

NATIVE_PROCESS_MINING_CONTRIBUTION_OR_REFINEMENT

Original form

Plural 1990s discovery approaches; explicit modelling assumptions in alpha, inductive, region-based and declarative methods. The reconstructed initial problem is: The output of an algorithm is mistaken for an unbiased reconstruction of the only process that could have generated the data.

Problem it addressed

The output of an algorithm is mistaken for an unbiased reconstruction of the only process that could have generated the data.

Failure mode it tries to prevent

The output of an algorithm is mistaken for an unbiased reconstruction of the only process that could have generated the data.

Mechanism

State the model language, search space, objective, noise handling and assumptions before interpreting discovered structure. Separate properties guaranteed by construction from properties inferred from the sample and from domain claims requiring external evidence.

Trigger or context

Any automatically or semi-automatically discovered process model.

Non trigger or cheap path

For a directly-follows summary, state that it is a relation summary and do not claim executable semantics or complete process recovery.

Dependencies or preconditions

Algorithm/version and parameter identity; knowledge of supported choices, loops, concurrency, silent transitions and data perspectives.

Domain profile
Event semantics and source provenance

Discovery assumes an event vocabulary whose activity meanings have been established; it does not discover those meanings from labels alone.

Case or object notion

Case-centric traces or object participation determine the basic input relation and therefore the recoverable structure.

Extraction abstraction and ordering

Abstraction, total-order choices and filtering are part of the inductive bias; retain their effect on the discovered model.

Log completeness noise and selection

Noise and incomplete sampling alter observed order relations; infrequent does not mean invalid, and absent does not mean impossible.

Model class and discovery assumptions

Central: disclose model class, algorithm, objective, parameters and scoped guarantees; preserve guarded alternatives rather than selecting a universal winner. Record-specific application: The output of an algorithm is mistaken for an unbiased reconstruction of the only process that could have generated the data. Each model is accompanied by a scoped claim: what it represents, what its construction guarantees and what remains hypothetical.

Reference model and conformance semantics

A discovered model is descriptive unless separately authorised. Using it as a reference does not make its inferred constraints obligations.

Fitness precision generalisation and simplicity

Use frequency-sensitive dependency estimates and thresholds to obtain a useful model; disclose threshold choices and inspect the behaviour removed or changed. Re-evaluate material low-frequency paths rather than classifying all of them as noise.

Original form

Fuzzy Mining’s 2007 significance/correlation-based abstraction for complex process maps. The reconstructed initial problem is: Dense maps overwhelm the consumer, but hiding edges may falsely imply that removed behaviour is impossible.

Problem it addressed

Dense maps overwhelm the consumer, but hiding edges may falsely imply that removed behaviour is impossible.

Failure mode it tries to prevent

Dense maps overwhelm the consumer, but hiding edges may falsely imply that removed behaviour is impossible.

Mechanism

Simplify a process view according to its communicative purpose, retain access to suppressed detail, and label the result as an abstraction rather than a complete executable specification. Test whether the consumer can answer the intended question.

Trigger or context

The full view is too dense for a specified diagnostic or communication task.

Non trigger or cheap path

Filter a small relevant segment, annotate a few events or use a table rather than adopting a large map-building ritual.

Dependencies or preconditions

A named task and consumer; explicit filtering/aggregation rules; recoverable detail.

Domain profile
Event semantics and source provenance

Discovery assumes an event vocabulary whose activity meanings have been established; it does not discover those meanings from labels alone.

Case or object notion

Case-centric traces or object participation determine the basic input relation and therefore the recoverable structure.

Extraction abstraction and ordering

Abstraction, total-order choices and filtering are part of the inductive bias; retain their effect on the discovered model.

Log completeness noise and selection

Noise and incomplete sampling alter observed order relations; infrequent does not mean invalid, and absent does not mean impossible.

Model class and discovery assumptions

Central: disclose model class, algorithm, objective, parameters and scoped guarantees; preserve guarded alternatives rather than selecting a universal winner. Record-specific application: Dense maps overwhelm the consumer, but hiding edges may falsely imply that removed behaviour is impossible. The consumer can identify the represented scope and retrieve material suppressed behaviour.

Reference model and conformance semantics

A discovered model is descriptive unless separately authorised. Using it as a reference does not make its inferred constraints obligations.

Fitness precision generalisation and simplicity

Evaluate fitness, precision, generalisation and simplicity separately and with applicable measures; a miner’s objective is not a complete validation.

Temporal validity and drift

A discovered model describes a dated observation regime; changed behaviour or logging can invalidate its previous scope.

Prediction causality and intervention boundary

Recovered control flow is not automatically causal structure. A model useful for replay need not be adequate for intervention prediction.

Human validation privacy and decision consumer

Participants test interpretation and useful abstraction; richer discovery is warranted only when a consumer can use its distinctions.

The consumer can identify the represented scope and retrieve material suppressed behaviour.

Lineage class

NATIVE_PROCESS_MINING_CONTRIBUTION_OR_REFINEMENT

Original form

Interactive analysis and domain interpretation in industrial mining and practitioner studies. The reconstructed initial problem is: Automated discovery omits knowledge of recording practices and intended distinctions, while unrecorded expert edits can disguise speculation as observation.

Problem it addressed

Automated discovery omits knowledge of recording practices and intended distinctions, while unrecorded expert edits can disguise speculation as observation.

Failure mode it tries to prevent

Automated discovery omits knowledge of recording practices and intended distinctions, while unrecorded expert edits can disguise speculation as observation.

Mechanism

Use domain knowledge to propose constraints, abstractions or candidate interpretations, label its origin and test its consequences against event evidence. Keep observed, inferred and prescribed statements separate when adjusting a model.

Trigger or context

Multiple plausible interpretations, incomprehensible models, unlogged activities or known policies materially affect the inquiry.

Non trigger or cheap path

A focused conversation about one ambiguous event class may suffice; a standing modelling committee is unnecessary.

Dependencies or preconditions

Access to relevant participants, explicit provenance for added knowledge and an opportunity to challenge it.

Domain profile
Event semantics and source provenance

Discovery assumes an event vocabulary whose activity meanings have been established; it does not discover those meanings from labels alone.

Case or object notion

Case-centric traces or object participation determine the basic input relation and therefore the recoverable structure.

Extraction abstraction and ordering

Abstraction, total-order choices and filtering are part of the inductive bias; retain their effect on the discovered model.

Log completeness noise and selection

Noise and incomplete sampling alter observed order relations; infrequent does not mean invalid, and absent does not mean impossible.

Model class and discovery assumptions

Central: disclose model class, algorithm, objective, parameters and scoped guarantees; preserve guarded alternatives rather than selecting a universal winner. Record-specific application: Automated discovery omits knowledge of recording practices and intended distinctions, while unrecorded expert edits can disguise speculation as observation. A consumer can tell which parts of the model were mined, interpreted or supplied as intended behaviour.

Reference model and conformance semantics

A discovered model is descriptive unless separately authorised. Using it as a reference does not make its inferred constraints obligations.

Fitness precision generalisation and simplicity

Evaluate fitness, precision, generalisation and simplicity separately and with applicable measures; a miner’s objective is not a complete validation.

Temporal validity and drift

A discovered model describes a dated observation regime; changed behaviour or logging can invalidate its previous scope.

Prediction causality and intervention boundary

Recovered control flow is not automatically causal structure. A model useful for replay need not be adequate for intervention prediction.

Human validation privacy and decision consumer

Participants test interpretation and useful abstraction; richer discovery is warranted only when a consumer can use its distinctions.

Expected engineering payoff
Claim

A consumer can tell which parts of the model were mined, interpreted or supplied as intended behaviour.

Status

EXPECTED_OR_LOGICALLY_REQUIRED_FOR_THE_STATED_CLAIM_NOT_A_UNIVERSAL_MEASURED_BENEFIT

Historical origin

Conformance checking compares event behaviour with an existing model; responsibility critiques clarify the status of that model.

Lineage class

NATIVE_PROCESS_MINING_CONTRIBUTION_OR_REFINEMENT

Original form

Conformance checking compares event behaviour with an existing model; responsibility critiques clarify the status of that model. The reconstructed initial problem is: A deviation score is treated as a violation without establishing who authorised the reference or what kind of claim it represents.

Problem it addressed

A deviation score is treated as a violation without establishing who authorised the reference or what kind of claim it represents.

Failure mode it tries to prevent

A deviation score is treated as a violation without establishing who authorised the reference or what kind of claim it represents.

Mechanism

Record whether the reference is descriptive, intended, contractual, technical or otherwise externally authorised; identify its version, scope and approving actor. Limit conformance conclusions to the actual reference semantics and route normative judgements to the actor entitled to make them.

Trigger or context

Any use of conformance to evaluate people, compliance, policy adherence, implementation or process correctness.

Non trigger or cheap path

For a purely descriptive comparison, say that the log differs from a model and make no normative allegation.

Dependencies or preconditions

An identifiable reference and scope; known abstraction; separate evidence for any external obligation.

Domain profile
Event semantics and source provenance

Event meaning and model activity mapping must agree at the relevant level; an unlogged manual activity can create apparent non-conformance.

Case or object notion

The reference and log must use compatible case/object semantics; trace comparisons can miss cross-case obligations.

Extraction abstraction and ordering

Ordering and abstraction determine which moves are compared; conversion must not silently turn uncertain order into certain violation.

Log completeness noise and selection

Missing, duplicate or selected events are rival explanations for mismatch; log defects and process defects are not the same conclusion.

Model class and discovery assumptions

Discovery is optional: the reference can be supplied independently. Formalisms define the behaviours and constraints the checker can compare.

Reference model and conformance semantics

Central: identify reference origin, version, authority, move semantics, costs and approximation; comparison is not normative authorisation. Record-specific application: A deviation score is treated as a violation without establishing who authorised the reference or what kind of claim it represents. Every material deviation states what it deviates from and the authority, if any, behind that reference.

Fitness precision generalisation and simplicity

Fitness measures observed correspondence; precision and other dimensions answer different questions and cannot be inferred from an optimal alignment.

Temporal validity and drift

Version reference expectations and observation windows; a changed descriptive model must not silently amend an obligation.

Prediction causality and intervention boundary

A deviation suggests diagnostic questions, not a causal remedy. Changing a process or rule requires separate evidence and authority.

Human validation privacy and decision consumer

Communicate alternative explanations to relevant participants and reference owners; people-related allegations need contestable, bounded evidence.

Expected engineering payoff
Claim

Every material deviation states what it deviates from and the authority, if any, behind that reference.

Status

EXPECTED_OR_LOGICALLY_REQUIRED_FOR_THE_STATED_CLAIM_NOT_A_UNIVERSAL_MEASURED_BENEFIT

For a purely descriptive comparison, say that the log differs from a model and make no normative allegation.

Decision or consumer

The reference owner and relevant institutional authority determine obligations. The mining analyst establishes a comparison, not legality or fairness.

Actor and authority boundary

Analyst computes correspondence; externally entitled actors interpret or amend obligations. No legal ruling or institutional power is inferred from mining.

Communication or interaction requirement

Communicate the reference origin, comparison semantics and rival explanations of mismatch to participants and actors entitled to choose a remedy. Specific receiving decision: The reference owner and relevant institutional authority determine obligations. The mining analyst establishes a comparison, not legality or fairness.

Observable postcondition

Every material deviation states what it deviates from and the authority, if any, behind that reference.

A discovered model can normalise the majority’s improper behaviour. An approved model may be obsolete, ambiguous or illegitimately imposed.

Historical origin

Token-based replay and fitness diagnostics in conformance checking.

Lineage class

NATIVE_PROCESS_MINING_CONTRIBUTION_OR_REFINEMENT

Original form

Token-based replay and fitness diagnostics in conformance checking. The reconstructed initial problem is: A numerical fitness score fails to show where observed events require missing tokens or leave residual tokens.

Problem it addressed

A numerical fitness score fails to show where observed events require missing tokens or leave residual tokens.

Failure mode it tries to prevent

A numerical fitness score fails to show where observed events require missing tokens or leave residual tokens.

Mechanism

Replay a trace under stated net and mapping semantics, expose missing/remaining-token diagnostics and identify artificial token insertion or other replay choices. Use the result as a bounded explanation of mismatch, not as a unique cause of failure.

Trigger or context

A Petri-net-style reference and log permit useful low-cost replay diagnostics.

Non trigger or cheap path

For a simple precedence rule, a direct trace check may be clearer and cheaper than a replay engine.

Dependencies or preconditions

Compatible model and event vocabulary; treatment of invisible transitions, duplicate labels and incomplete traces.

Domain profile
Event semantics and source provenance

Event meaning and model activity mapping must agree at the relevant level; an unlogged manual activity can create apparent non-conformance.

Case or object notion

The reference and log must use compatible case/object semantics; trace comparisons can miss cross-case obligations.

Extraction abstraction and ordering

Ordering and abstraction determine which moves are compared; conversion must not silently turn uncertain order into certain violation.

Log completeness noise and selection

Missing, duplicate or selected events are rival explanations for mismatch; log defects and process defects are not the same conclusion.

Model class and discovery assumptions

Discovery is optional: the reference can be supplied independently. Formalisms define the behaviours and constraints the checker can compare.

Reference model and conformance semantics

Central: identify reference origin, version, authority, move semantics, costs and approximation; comparison is not normative authorisation. Record-specific application: A numerical fitness score fails to show where observed events require missing tokens or leave residual tokens. The consumer can identify which replay assumptions and token discrepancies produced the result.

Fitness precision generalisation and simplicity

Fitness measures observed correspondence; precision and other dimensions answer different questions and cannot be inferred from an optimal alignment.

Temporal validity and drift

Version reference expectations and observation windows; a changed descriptive model must not silently amend an obligation.

Prediction causality and intervention boundary

A deviation suggests diagnostic questions, not a causal remedy. Changing a process or rule requires separate evidence and authority.

Human validation privacy and decision consumer

Communicate alternative explanations to relevant participants and reference owners; people-related allegations need contestable, bounded evidence.

Expected engineering payoff
Claim

The consumer can identify which replay assumptions and token discrepancies produced the result.

EXPECTED_OR_LOGICALLY_REQUIRED_FOR_THE_STATED_CLAIM_NOT_A_UNIVERSAL_MEASURED_BENEFIT

Lineage class

NATIVE_PROCESS_MINING_CONTRIBUTION_OR_REFINEMENT

Original form

Uncertain-event conformance using sets of possible realisations in 2019. The reconstructed initial problem is: An analyst either invents a single complete trace or refuses all analysis when activity, event presence or time is uncertain.

Problem it addressed

An analyst either invents a single complete trace or refuses all analysis when activity, event presence or time is uncertain.

Failure mode it tries to prevent

An analyst either invents a single complete trace or refuses all analysis when activity, event presence or time is uncertain.

Mechanism

Represent the admitted event uncertainties and compute or approximate lower and upper conformance costs across supported realisations. Report what holds for all, some or none of those realisations without assigning unsupported probabilities.

Trigger or context

Material uncertainty is bounded well enough to express meaningful alternatives and conformance remains decision-relevant.

Non trigger or cheap path

Flag a local ambiguity or withhold the affected judgement when full realisation analysis would not change a decision.

Dependencies or preconditions

Defensible uncertainty sets, a compatible reference and a declared computational approximation.

Domain profile
Event semantics and source provenance

Event meaning and model activity mapping must agree at the relevant level; an unlogged manual activity can create apparent non-conformance.

Case or object notion

The reference and log must use compatible case/object semantics; trace comparisons can miss cross-case obligations.

Extraction abstraction and ordering

Ordering and abstraction determine which moves are compared; conversion must not silently turn uncertain order into certain violation.

Log completeness noise and selection

Missing, duplicate or selected events are rival explanations for mismatch; log defects and process defects are not the same conclusion.

Model class and discovery assumptions

Discovery is optional: the reference can be supplied independently. Formalisms define the behaviours and constraints the checker can compare.

Reference model and conformance semantics

Central: identify reference origin, version, authority, move semantics, costs and approximation; comparison is not normative authorisation. Record-specific application: An analyst either invents a single complete trace or refuses all analysis when activity, event presence or time is uncertain. A result distinguishes robust mismatch from mismatch that depends on an unresolved event interpretation.

Fitness precision generalisation and simplicity

Fitness measures observed correspondence; precision and other dimensions answer different questions and cannot be inferred from an optimal alignment.

Temporal validity and drift

Version reference expectations and observation windows; a changed descriptive model must not silently amend an obligation.

Prediction causality and intervention boundary

A deviation suggests diagnostic questions, not a causal remedy. Changing a process or rule requires separate evidence and authority.

Human validation privacy and decision consumer

Communicate alternative explanations to relevant participants and reference owners; people-related allegations need contestable, bounded evidence.

Expected engineering payoff
Claim

A result distinguishes robust mismatch from mismatch that depends on an unresolved event interpretation.

EPM-038 — Authorised model repair versus process correction

Property id

EPM-038

Property name

Authorised model repair versus process correction

Lineage id

EVOLVED_PROCESS_MINING

Candidate origin
Type

SOURCE_GROUNDED_MECHANISM_EXTRACTION

Family

PM4

Source ids

  • EPM-S047

  • EPM-S001

Note

Registered during the scoped research; unfavourable and duplicate candidates remain in the denominator.

Historical origin

Local model repair from alignments, contrasted with complete rediscovery.

Lineage class

NATIVE_PROCESS_MINING_CONTRIBUTION_OR_REFINEMENT

Original form

Local model repair from alignments, contrasted with complete rediscovery. The reconstructed initial problem is: A discrepancy triggers indiscriminate model replacement, or the reference is silently amended to make undesirable behaviour conform.

Problem it addressed

A discrepancy triggers indiscriminate model replacement, or the reference is silently amended to make undesirable behaviour conform.

Failure mode it tries to prevent

A discrepancy triggers indiscriminate model replacement, or the reference is silently amended to make undesirable behaviour conform.

Mechanism

Decide whether evidence supports correcting data, repairing a descriptive model, changing execution or formally revising an authorised rule. For model repair, preserve unaffected intent and re-evaluate changed behaviour; maintain the prior reference when continuity matters.

Trigger or context

Confirmed mismatch reveals an inadequate descriptive model or a legitimately approved change in intended behaviour.

Non trigger or cheap path

Correct one extraction rule or annotate one justified exception when this closes the issue; rediscovery is not obligatory.

Dependencies or preconditions

Established diagnosis, reference provenance, appropriate change authority and a comparison against the prior model.

Domain profile
Event semantics and source provenance

Event meaning and model activity mapping must agree at the relevant level; an unlogged manual activity can create apparent non-conformance.

Case or object notion

The reference and log must use compatible case/object semantics; trace comparisons can miss cross-case obligations.

Extraction abstraction and ordering

Ordering and abstraction determine which moves are compared; conversion must not silently turn uncertain order into certain violation.

Log completeness noise and selection

Missing, duplicate or selected events are rival explanations for mismatch; log defects and process defects are not the same conclusion.

Model class and discovery assumptions

Discovery is optional: the reference can be supplied independently. Formalisms define the behaviours and constraints the checker can compare.

Reference model and conformance semantics

Central: identify reference origin, version, authority, move semantics, costs and approximation; comparison is not normative authorisation. Record-specific application: A discrepancy triggers indiscriminate model replacement, or the reference is silently amended to make undesirable behaviour conform. The chosen correction has a supported cause, a stated change boundary and a checked effect on previously meaningful behaviour.

Fitness precision generalisation and simplicity

Fitness measures observed correspondence; precision and other dimensions answer different questions and cannot be inferred from an optimal alignment.

Temporal validity and drift

Version reference expectations and observation windows; a changed descriptive model must not silently amend an obligation.

Prediction causality and intervention boundary

A deviation suggests diagnostic questions, not a causal remedy. Changing a process or rule requires separate evidence and authority.

Human validation privacy and decision consumer

Communicate alternative explanations to relevant participants and reference owners; people-related allegations need contestable, bounded evidence.

Expected engineering payoff
Claim

The chosen correction has a supported cause, a stated change boundary and a checked effect on previously meaningful behaviour.

Status

EXPECTED_OR_LOGICALLY_REQUIRED_FOR_THE_STATED_CLAIM_NOT_A_UNIVERSAL_MEASURED_BENEFIT

Cost boundary

Correct one extraction rule or annotate one justified exception when this closes the issue; rediscovery is not obligatory.

Decision or consumer

Model maintainer can repair a descriptive model within mandate; changing an obligation requires its own authorised actor and process.

Actor and authority boundary

Model maintainer can repair a descriptive model within mandate; changing an obligation requires its own authorised actor and process. Analytical competence does not itself supply additional organisational authority.

Communication or interaction requirement

Communicate the reference origin, comparison semantics and rival explanations of mismatch to participants and actors entitled to choose a remedy. Specific receiving decision: Model maintainer can repair a descriptive model within mandate; changing an obligation requires its own authorised actor and process.

Observable postcondition

The chosen correction has a supported cause, a stated change boundary and a checked effect on previously meaningful behaviour.

Known failure modes

Local minimality can preserve a flawed global structure; fitting all observed traces can normalise wrongdoing. Smaller edits are not always the better repair.

Important criticisms
Assessment

Local minimality can preserve a flawed global structure; fitting all observed traces can normalise wrongdoing. Smaller edits are not always the better repair.

Historical origin

Fitness and appropriateness in conformance work; the Manifesto’s four quality dimensions; subsequent metric critiques.

Lineage class

NATIVE_PROCESS_MINING_CONTRIBUTION_OR_REFINEMENT

Original form

Fitness and appropriateness in conformance work; the Manifesto’s four quality dimensions; subsequent metric critiques. The reconstructed initial problem is: A model is selected because one score improves while important behaviour or interpretability deteriorates.

Problem it addressed

A model is selected because one score improves while important behaviour or interpretability deteriorates.

Failure mode it tries to prevent

A model is selected because one score improves while important behaviour or interpretability deteriorates.

Mechanism

Evaluate fitness, precision, generalisation and simplicity as distinct questions, naming each operational measure and its assumptions. Report trade-offs and missing measurements rather than compressing them into an unexplained total.

Trigger or context

Comparison, selection or validation of discovered or repaired process models.

Non trigger or cheap path

Evaluate only the dimensions material to a tightly bounded question, explaining exclusions instead of manufacturing a four-score dashboard.

Dependencies or preconditions

A defined task, model semantics, log population and measures whose preconditions are met.

Domain profile
Event semantics and source provenance

Evaluation on a syntactically valid log still depends on event semantics; model scores do not establish what was observed.

Case or object notion

Use cases, objects, prefixes or process generators as the unit appropriate to the claim; do not count dependent prefixes as independent cases.

Extraction abstraction and ordering

Fix or compare abstraction, order and preprocessing fairly; differences in preparation can dominate algorithm differences.

Log completeness noise and selection

Representativeness, noise, censoring and excluded runs change what an evaluation estimates.

Model class and discovery assumptions

Compare algorithms within declared model and output semantics; unsupported constructs and failed conversions are material outcomes.

Reference model and conformance semantics

Conformance-derived metrics require compatible reference semantics; descriptive model quality does not confer normative authority.

Fitness precision generalisation and simplicity

Central: separate the four questions, specify actual metrics and retain trade-offs, missing values and known formal weaknesses. Record-specific application: A model is selected because one score improves while important behaviour or interpretability deteriorates. A selection rationale states which trade-off was accepted and does not imply that a good score on one dimension establishes the others.

Temporal validity and drift

Match temporal splits to prospective claims and keep tuning information out of the future test regime.

Prediction causality and intervention boundary

Predictive scores, model quality and causal utility are different targets; none supplies the others without additional assumptions.

Human validation privacy and decision consumer

Consumer priorities justify local trade-offs; reproducibility and expert usability checks complement rather than replace empirical validity.

Expected engineering payoff
Claim

A selection rationale states which trade-off was accepted and does not imply that a good score on one dimension establishes the others.

Status

EXPECTED_OR_LOGICALLY_REQUIRED_FOR_THE_STATED_CLAIM_NOT_A_UNIVERSAL_MEASURED_BENEFIT

Cost boundary

Evaluate only the dimensions material to a tightly bounded question, explaining exclusions instead of manufacturing a four-score dashboard.

Decision or consumer

Analyst explains the measures; the consumer supplies the decision priorities rather than allowing a metric package to choose them.

Actor and authority boundary

Analyst explains the measures; the consumer supplies the decision priorities rather than allowing a metric package to choose them. Analytical competence does not itself supply additional organisational authority.

Communication or interaction requirement

Communicate experimental units, actual metric definitions, missing results and task-specific trade-offs rather than only an aggregate score. Specific receiving decision: Analyst explains the measures; the consumer supplies the decision priorities rather than allowing a metric package to choose them.

Observable postcondition

A selection rationale states which trade-off was accepted and does not imply that a good score on one dimension establishes the others.

Known failure modes

Different formal definitions can rank the same models differently; not every measure is defined or tractable for every model class.

Important criticisms
Assessment

Different formal definitions can rank the same models differently; not every measure is defined or tractable for every model class.

Failure mode it tries to prevent

Mechanism

Trigger or context

Precision influences model choice, claimed superiority or the rejection of a permissive model.

Non trigger or cheap path

For an obvious flower model or simple local question, an explicit behavioural counterexample may be clearer than a fragile aggregate metric.

Reference model and conformance semantics

Fitness precision generalisation and simplicity

Central: separate the four questions, specify actual metrics and retain trade-offs, missing values and known formal weaknesses. Record-specific application: A precision number is interpreted as a representation-invariant estimate of how much invalid behaviour a model permits. The reported precision result names what it measures and the important limitations that can change the ranking.

Property id

EPM-046

Property name

Elapsed time distinguished from effort

Lineage id

EVOLVED_PROCESS_MINING

Candidate origin

Source ids

Note

Historical origin

Performance annotation of process models, refined by timestamp-quality and fine-grained performance work.

Lineage class

NATIVE_PROCESS_MINING_CONTRIBUTION_OR_REFINEMENT

Original form

Performance annotation of process models, refined by timestamp-quality and fine-grained performance work. The reconstructed initial problem is: Elapsed time between events is reported as active effort or assigned to the wrong activity.

Problem it addressed

Elapsed time between events is reported as active effort or assigned to the wrong activity.

Failure mode it tries to prevent

Elapsed time between events is reported as active effort or assigned to the wrong activity.

Mechanism

Define each duration by its observed endpoints and lifecycle semantics; distinguish throughput, waiting, service and unobserved time. Attribute elapsed intervals only where the data and model support the attribution, and retain missing intervals as missing.

Trigger or context

Any timing result used to diagnose delay, compare resources or change staffing.

Non trigger or cheap path

Report a milestone-to-milestone elapsed interval without claiming a service-time decomposition when start or enablement events are unavailable.

Dependencies or preconditions

Reliable endpoint meaning, ordering and handling of incomplete cases; awareness of calendars and batch recording.

Domain profile
Event semantics and source provenance

Timestamp and resource fields must be interpreted as recording semantics, not automatically as effort or person identity.

Case or object notion

Case/object relations determine which intervals and interactions belong together; shared events can distort flattened duration and rework.

Extraction abstraction and ordering

Lifecycle pairing, calendars, batching and ordering are necessary for stronger duration claims; preserve omitted phases.

Log completeness noise and selection

Censoring, incomplete cases, unlogged prerequisites and selective resource capture affect performance attribution.

Model class and discovery assumptions

A descriptive process map may be sufficient; executable or simulation models add assumptions that need separate validation.

Reference model and conformance semantics

Performance deviation from a target is not proof of a violated obligation or culpable worker; the reference target requires interpretation.

Fitness precision generalisation and simplicity

Fitness can support replay but cannot validate timing semantics or organisational explanations. Human interpretability is a separate requirement.

Temporal validity and drift

Compare like periods and distinguish demand/case-mix changes from performance changes; dates and source regimes matter.

Prediction causality and intervention boundary

Pattern, cause, feasible remedy and measured consequence are separate claims; intervention benefit requires evidence beyond delay localisation.

Human validation privacy and decision consumer

Operational participants validate omitted context and resource meaning; privacy, fairness and a real decision consumer constrain personal attribution. Record-specific application: Elapsed time between events is reported as active effort or assigned to the wrong activity. A duration claim can be traced to its endpoints and does not silently equate elapsed time with labour.

Expected engineering payoff
Claim

A duration claim can be traced to its endpoints and does not silently equate elapsed time with labour.

Status

EXPECTED_OR_LOGICALLY_REQUIRED_FOR_THE_STATED_CLAIM_NOT_A_UNIVERSAL_MEASURED_BENEFIT

Report a milestone-to-milestone elapsed interval without claiming a service-time decomposition when start or enablement events are unavailable.

Actor and authority boundary

Performance analyst and operational staff agree what the time measure denotes before it is used as evidence of effort or blame. Analytical competence does not itself supply additional organisational authority.

Communication or interaction requirement

Exchange traceable intervals and interaction patterns with operational participants; distinguish observed facts, proposed causes, agreed actions and consequences. Specific receiving decision: Performance analyst and operational staff agree what the time measure denotes before it is used as evidence of effort or blame.

Observable postcondition

A duration claim can be traced to its endpoints and does not silently equate elapsed time with labour.

Problem it addressed

Case-local averages hide shared resources, batching, overtaking, demand variation or synchronisation with other objects.

Mechanism

Include inter-case or inter-object context when it materially affects the interpretation of queues and delays; stratify or annotate by relevant load, batching and relation states. Keep inferred context distinct from directly observed resource states.

Trigger or context

Observed delay depends on shared resources, priority rules, batches or multiple interacting objects.

Compare like periods and distinguish demand/case-mix changes from performance changes; dates and source regimes matter.

Pattern, cause, feasible remedy and measured consequence are separate claims; intervention benefit requires evidence beyond delay localisation.

Human validation privacy and decision consumer

Operational participants validate omitted context and resource meaning; privacy, fairness and a real decision consumer constrain personal attribution. Original form

Context-aware performance analysis intersecting with responsible mining and selection-bias critique. The reconstructed initial problem is: Differences between groups, periods or resources are attributed to competence despite different case mix, priorities or observation windows.

Problem it addressed

Differences between groups, periods or resources are attributed to competence despite different case mix, priorities or observation windows.

Failure mode it tries to prevent

Differences between groups, periods or resources are attributed to competence despite different case mix, priorities or observation windows.

Mechanism

Compare like with like where possible, disclose subgroup and case-mix differences, and examine how selection, censoring and task allocation affect the result. When comparability fails, narrow the claim instead of normalising away inconvenient differences.

Trigger or context

Performance comparisons across people, units, time periods, demographic groups or process variants.

Non trigger or cheap path

Report separate descriptive distributions or refrain from ranking rather than fit an unjustified adjustment model.

Dependencies or preconditions

Relevant context variables, sufficient subgroup support and a clear target estimand; sensitive attributes require particular justification.

Domain profile

Lifecycle pairing, calendars, batching and ordering are necessary for stronger duration claims; preserve omitted phases.

A descriptive process map may be sufficient; executable or simulation models add assumptions that need separate validation.

Reference model and conformance semantics

Performance deviation from a target is not proof of a violated obligation or culpable worker; the reference target requires interpretation.

Fitness precision generalisation and simplicity

Fitness can support replay but cannot validate timing semantics or organisational explanations. Human interpretability is a separate requirement.

Temporal validity and drift

Compare like periods and distinguish demand/case-mix changes from performance changes; dates and source regimes matter.

Prediction causality and intervention boundary

Pattern, cause, feasible remedy and measured consequence are separate claims; intervention benefit requires evidence beyond delay localisation.

Human validation privacy and decision consumer

Operational participants validate omitted context and resource meaning; privacy, fairness and a real decision consumer constrain personal attribution. Record-specific application: Differences between groups, periods or resources are attributed to competence despite different case mix, priorities or observation windows. A bounded explanation or confirmation that no change is needed can be a valid result; another dashboard is not obligatory.

Omit or retire this mechanism when its trigger no longer holds, a cheaper adequate path meets the stated postcondition, or the intended consumer disappears; preserve evidence needed for existing consequential decisions. Historical origin

Streaming discovery and conformance under bounded memory and partial traces.

Lineage class

NATIVE_PROCESS_MINING_CONTRIBUTION_OR_REFINEMENT

Original form

Streaming discovery and conformance under bounded memory and partial traces. The reconstructed initial problem is: An online model silently forgets older behaviour or treats incomplete running cases as finished deviations.

Problem it addressed

An online model silently forgets older behaviour or treats incomplete running cases as finished deviations.

Failure mode it tries to prevent

An online model silently forgets older behaviour or treats incomplete running cases as finished deviations.

Mechanism

Specify window/forgetting policy, event arrival order, late-data handling and prefix semantics; expose the trade-off between latency, memory and historical coverage. Assess partial-case conformance as partial rather than pretending the case has ended.

Trigger or context

Data volume or required latency makes bounded online processing preferable to complete batch analysis.

Non trigger or cheap path

Periodic batch analysis with explicit windows is adequate when near-real-time decisions are unnecessary.

Dependencies or preconditions

Event-stream semantics, resource budget, state retention policy and support for incomplete cases.

Domain profile
Event semantics and source provenance

Changes in event meaning and recording behaviour are possible drift causes and must be investigated.

Case or object notion

Case or object correlation changes can alter apparent process behaviour without changing work.

Extraction abstraction and ordering

Version transformations, label abstraction and arrival ordering; late events and partial traces require explicit treatment.

Log completeness noise and selection

Sampling, noise and incomplete cases affect alarms; a stream window is not the whole historical population.

Model class and discovery assumptions

Adaptive discovery is one response, not a mandatory consequence of every detected shift.

Reference model and conformance semantics

Keep descriptive model revision distinct from authorised reference revision; drift does not itself amend obligations.

Fitness precision generalisation and simplicity

Evaluate detector delay, false alarms and feature sensitivity separately from model-quality scores.

Temporal validity and drift

Central: define observation windows, regimes, forgetting, recurrence and revision continuity; distinguish abrupt, gradual and other material change patterns. Record-specific application: An online model silently forgets older behaviour or treats incomplete running cases as finished deviations. An online result states what history it represents and how partial/late observations affect it.

Prediction causality and intervention boundary

Distribution shift can invalidate prediction or causal-policy evaluation; detection is not a causal explanation or action warrant.

Human validation privacy and decision consumer

A consumer must be able to investigate and act on alarms; excessive churn and alert burden are real costs.

Expected engineering payoff
Claim

An online result states what history it represents and how partial/late observations affect it.

Status

EXPECTED_OR_LOGICALLY_REQUIRED_FOR_THE_STATED_CLAIM_NOT_A_UNIVERSAL_MEASURED_BENEFIT

Retain uncertainty-aware support as an assumption-sensitive import, not a universal reliability wrapper. The sepsis study reuses one modest static dataset and disclaims deployment readiness. Conformal marginal coverage does not require accurate base probabilities, and it does not establish per-case conditional safety under arbitrary drift.

Original form

Outcome monitoring extended to prescriptive decisions under limited intervention resources. The reconstructed initial problem is: A predictor improves a benchmark score after the useful intervention window has closed or recommends more actions than resources permit.

Problem it addressed

A predictor improves a benchmark score after the useful intervention window has closed or recommends more actions than resources permit.

Failure mode it tries to prevent

A predictor improves a benchmark score after the useful intervention window has closed or recommends more actions than resources permit.

Mechanism

Evaluate predictive utility at actual decision times, accounting for lead time, false alarms, intervention capacity and opportunity cost. Choose thresholds or policies against an explicit decision objective rather than accuracy alone.

Trigger or context

Predictions are intended to allocate attention, resources or interventions to running cases.

Non trigger or cheap path

A simple prioritisation rule may be adequate, or no prediction is warranted if no timely action is possible.

Dependencies or preconditions

A feasible action set, costs, resource constraints, decision times and an explicit baseline policy.

Domain profile
Event semantics and source provenance

Feature meanings and update times must be established; a final case attribute may not have existed at prediction time.

Case or object notion

Use the correct case, prefix, object context or decision occasion; account for dependence and resource coupling.

Extraction abstraction and ordering

Prevent future-derived aggregation and label leakage; preserve the state actually observable at each decision occasion.

Log completeness noise and selection

Completed-case selection, censoring, class imbalance and support for actions affect evaluation and causal identification.

Model class and discovery assumptions

Predictive models need not be discovered process models; their architecture and information access must be compared fairly.

Reference model and conformance semantics

A reference process can constrain feasible actions but prediction does not validate its normative authority.

Fitness precision generalisation and simplicity

Evaluate predictive discrimination, calibration, coverage, timing, cost and decision utility for their distinct purposes; a process fitness score is not predictive utility.

Temporal validity and drift

Use a split and calibration regime matching prospective use; drift and intervention feedback can invalidate earlier results.

Prediction causality and intervention boundary

Central: distinguish prediction, explanation, causal identification, feasible advice, authorised action and measured effect. A claimed useful prediction has an available response and an evaluation matched to its timing and resource constraints.

Original form

Process adaptation and sequential intervention research expose feedback between recommendations, behaviour and later data. The reconstructed initial problem is: A policy changes the process while its old benchmark score continues to be reported as if the data-generating regime were unchanged.

Problem it addressed

A policy changes the process while its old benchmark score continues to be reported as if the data-generating regime were unchanged.

Failure mode it tries to prevent

A policy changes the process while its old benchmark score continues to be reported as if the data-generating regime were unchanged.

Mechanism

Record when recommendations or interventions alter exposure, action selection or outcomes; reassess predictive, calibration and causal claims against the new regime. Preserve the prior evaluation as historical evidence and explicitly test the revised policy or narrow its use.

Trigger or context

Advice is acted upon, a policy is deployed, or user adaptation materially changes the process that produced training data.

Non trigger or cheap path

For unused exploratory predictions, no intervention-driven re-evaluation is needed beyond ordinary temporal checks.

Dependencies or preconditions

Intervention and policy version identity, action/outcome observation, a comparison design and a consumer able to revise or suspend use.

Domain profile
Event semantics and source provenance

Feature meanings and update times must be established; a final case attribute may not have existed at prediction time.

Case or object notion

Use the correct case, prefix, object context or decision occasion; account for dependence and resource coupling.

Extraction abstraction and ordering

Prevent future-derived aggregation and label leakage; preserve the state actually observable at each decision occasion.

Log completeness noise and selection

Completed-case selection, censoring, class imbalance and support for actions affect evaluation and causal identification.

Model class and discovery assumptions

Predictive models need not be discovered process models; their architecture and information access must be compared fairly.

Reference model and conformance semantics

A reference process can constrain feasible actions but prediction does not validate its normative authority.

Fitness precision generalisation and simplicity

Evaluate predictive discrimination, calibration, coverage, timing, cost and decision utility for their distinct purposes; a process fitness score is not predictive utility.

Temporal validity and drift

Use a split and calibration regime matching prospective use; drift and intervention feedback can invalidate earlier results.

Prediction causality and intervention boundary

Central: distinguish prediction, explanation, causal identification, feasible advice, authorised action and measured effect. Record-specific application: A policy changes the process while its old benchmark score continues to be reported as if the data-generating regime were unchanged. Post-intervention claims cite evidence from the relevant regime and do not recycle an invalidated pre-intervention evaluation.

Human validation privacy and decision consumer

Human review and abstention need an actual recipient and capacity; sensitive features, fairness and action consequences require accountable decisions.

Expected engineering payoff
Claim

Post-intervention claims cite evidence from the relevant regime and do not recycle an invalidated pre-intervention evaluation.

EXPECTED_OR_LOGICALLY_REQUIRED_FOR_THE_STATED_CLAIM_NOT_A_UNIVERSAL_MEASURED_BENEFIT
